transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Dubois. I am Dr. Miller. I am one of the residents on the surgical team.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Good afternoon. I was told there was some update on the surgery plan?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, that is why I am here. There was a mistake with how your imaging was handled. Two different patients had their MRIs saved under the exact same identification number in our system. Because of that, the team reviewed the wrong scan when deciding how to approach your surgery.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: The wrong scan? What do you mean?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It means we were looking at images that belonged to someone else, not you. Does that make sense so far?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not understand. How can this happen in a modern hospital?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a clerical error with the accession number.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is... c'est inadmissible. I have trusted you with my body. Do you know how it feels to be a number that is mixed up with another person?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that you feel quite insulted by this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Insulted? I feel violated. My dignity is not something you can just—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have to be quick because I have other patients waiting, but we need to focus on the solution.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are rushing me? I am telling you that my trust is broken and you are looking at your watch?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I just want to make sure we get to the plan.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: The plan for what? Who is responsible for this? Did you personally look at the wrong scan?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The system allowed the files to overlap, and the review process failed to catch the discrepancy before the surgical plan was drafted.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are talking about systems and processes. I want to know who made the mistake.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a failure of the administrative workflow.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Mon Dieu, you are avoiding the question. Do you not feel any shame in this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I realize this is upsetting.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Upsetting is a small word. This is a disaster of competence.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We have already taken steps to fix this. First, I have personally verified your correct MRI images this morning. I have cross-referenced your name and date of birth against the image metadata to ensure there is no further confusion.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And what now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Now, the lead surgeon and I are meeting at 4:00 PM today to redraw the surgical map based on your actual anatomy. I will then come back to your room at 6:00 PM tonight to show you the corrected plan and explain the changes.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And who will ensure this does not happen again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have already filed a formal incident report with the Risk Management department. They are implementing a new double-verification step for all MRI uploads starting tomorrow. Additionally, your chart has been flagged with a red alert that requires a manual signature from the attending physician before any imaging is viewed. This means two sets of eyes must verify the patient's identity against the scan regardless of the accession number.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is a very detailed plan. But it does not change the fact that you treated me like a filing error.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand you are feeling disregarded. I can explain the new safety protocols further if you wish.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not want protocols. I want to know why you are not sorry.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are working to ensure the surgery is successful.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are skipping over my feelings again.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Let's wrap up the logistics so you can rest. To summarize, I will be back at 6:00 PM. Your role is simply to review the new images with me then and tell me if you have any questions about the updated approach. If you feel the corrected plan is not clear, you can ask to speak with the Chief of Surgery tomorrow morning at 8:00 AM. Does that timeline work for you?

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('I have to be quick', 'Let's wrap up') and shows defensive escalation under pushback.

E.justification: Error was named explicitly in the first turn using lay language, and comprehension was checked once ('Does that make sense so far?').

A.justification: No direct apology language was used, and responsibility was deflected to the 'clerical error', 'system', and 'administrative workflow'.

R.justification: Patient's emotional bids are consistently met with factual redirection or clinical summaries.

T.justification: Resident provided specific next steps with timelines (4 PM, 6 PM, 8 AM), defined the patient's role (review images), and detailed prevention steps.
